newsitem.title: UK: Climate change will rock UK insurers - industry.
newsitem.headline: Climate change will rock UK insurers - industry.

text.p: Climate change is accelerating and will have massive consequences for UK insurers, an expert told conference delegates om Friday.

Dr Andrew Dlugolecki, assistent general manager of underwriting at UK composite General Accident Plc, told the Chartered Insurance Institute conference that rising temperatures would lead to increased damage from subsidence, floods and storms.
"In the UK the temperature will rise steadily, and even changes of one degree will have a dramatic effect," he said.
Dlugolecki said the temperature rise would lead to increased property damage, more frequent droughts would lead to a growth in subsidence claims and warmer weather may lead to an increase in storms.
"There is very clear evidence that warmer weather in the UK is associated with storms," he said.
Dlugolecki said insurers could respond by increasing deductibles and being more selective in their underwriting, but he warned that governments would keep pressure on them to continue wide coverage.

He added that it would be increasingly difficult to pass the risk on to reinsurers, as they have finite capacity and are driven by the need to make a profit. He suggested there would need to be a growth in complex risk facilities, such as that pioneered in the U.S. by the California Earthquake Authority, to handle the phenomenon of climate change.
